brief: Daily flow note; clearest chains: Micron beat and raised (revenue $54.2bn vs $50.9bn consensus, guide $61.50bn midpoint vs $57.6bn consensus) on tight DRAM/NAND supply-demand through 2027-2028 and 10 new long-term agreements covering ~35% of expected FY30 revenue; GS reads the agreements as support for a higher multiple on peak earnings and raises its price target to $1250 from $1100. On the Fed, August core PCE rose 0.25% m/m, 3.01% yoy versus 3.4% expected, so GS cuts its Q4/Q4 core PCE forecast to 3.0% (below the FOMC median of 3.4%); with NY Fed's Williams saying there is no need for urgency, GS pushes its forecast second hike to December and sees a strong chance of no further hikes, even as the market prices only 36% odds of an October hike and the 10yr sits at 5.28%. Bitcoin rallied +43% in Q3 despite higher yields, oil and Middle East tensions, which GS ties to ETF inflows and now calls technically constructive. Gold: GS cuts its year-end target to $4650 from $4900 on rate-driven ETF demand but keeps its 2027 target at $5400 on central-bank buying. Remaining items (bond-proxy idea, DoorDash drones, software fundamentals, OpenAI funding, money-market balances) are reported, not argued.
